newsitem.title: UK: London precious metals drift but PGMs volatile.
newsitem.headline: London precious metals drift but PGMs volatile.

text.p: Precious metal prices drifted lower on Wednesday afternoon after a frantic couple of hours in the platinum group metals (PGMs) and fairly heavy selling of gold earlier, dealers said.
Most of the early action centred on covering palladium positions in a market where available stocks are either non-existent or tightly held.

"There was another round of borrowing in palladium this morning which drove the market crazy. But after about an hour in which everybody did what they had to do, they decided that was it and it has been quiet since," one dealer said.

Dealers aid one month rates were out to between 150 and 180 percent for Zurich good delivery plate and lenders of platinum where tightness was less biting were achieving rates of around 60 percent for a month.
Palladium fixed at an all-time high since fixings began in 1989 of $210 per ounce this morning, its highest spot price since 1980, and platinum made $425, a 16-month high fix.
By the 1300 GMT fixing, palladium was off $2.00 at $208.00 and platinum was at $419.00.

Both metals have soared since the start of the year - palladium is up 85 percent from the year's low and platinum is up 25 percent - due to administrative delays in Russian supplies to key importer Japan.
Russia is the world's biggest producer of palladium and is second to South Africa in platinum output.
"There is a fundamental reason for palladium being tight but platinum shouldn't be that short. It looks like somebody is trying to squeeze it," a dealer said.

Dealers noted ironically there was no tightness in Johnson-Matthey refined sponge grade palladium avalable in London but hedging any purchase was impossible on the discounted Nymex futures or in the tight Zurich market.
"That means you have to offer the customer a discount which sounds ridiculous," one PGM dealer said.
Gold absorbed significant selling ealier as the row between the German Ministry of Finance and the Bundesbank over revaluing gold reserves reached a compromise.
It found support just under $341.00 to fix at 1400 GMT at $341.75 down 65 cents from the morning.
Silver was indicated at $4.74/$4.76 up a cent but dealers noted that forward rates in the metal were still tight as some speculative interest switched there from the overcooked PGMs.
